component.ComponentContext:
ComponentContext represents the evaluated context for rendering component resources.
This is the output of BuildComponentContext and is used by the template engine.
component.ComponentContext.configurations:
Configurations are extracted configuration items from workload.
Contains configs and secrets for the single container.
Accessed via ${configurations.configs.envs}, ${configurations.secrets.files}, etc.
component.ComponentContext.dataplane:
DataPlane provides data plane configuration.
Accessed via ${dataplane.secretStore}, ${dataplane.gateway.ingress.external.https.host}, etc.
component.ComponentContext.dependencies:
Dependencies contains dependency metadata and merged env vars for templates.
Accessed via ${dependencies.items} and ${dependencies.envVars}.
component.ComponentContext.derived: Derived holds precomputed views that CEL macros resolve to via field selects.
component.ComponentContext.environment:
Environment provides environment-specific gateway configuration.
Accessed via ${environment.gateway.ingress.external.https.host}, etc.
Falls back to DataPlane gateway values if Environment.Gateway is not configured.
component.ComponentContext.environmentConfigs:
EnvironmentConfigs from ReleaseBinding.Spec.ComponentTypeEnvironmentConfigs, pruned to ComponentType.Spec.EnvironmentConfigs schema.
Accessed via ${environmentConfigs.*}
component.ComponentContext.gateway:
Gateway provides the effective gateway configuration for this deployment.
Uses environment gateway if configured, falls back to DataPlane gateway.
Accessed via ${gateway.ingress.external.https.host}, etc.
component.ComponentContext.metadata:
Metadata provides structured naming and labeling information.
Accessed via ${metadata.name}, ${metadata.namespace}, ${metadata.componentName}, etc.
component.ComponentContext.parameters:
Parameters from Component.Spec.Parameters, pruned to ComponentType.Spec.Parameters schema.
Accessed via ${parameters.*}
component.ComponentContext.workload:
Workload contains workload specification (container, endpoints, connections).
Accessed via ${workload.container}, ${workload.endpoints}, etc.
component.ComponentContextInput: ComponentContextInput contains all inputs needed to build a component rendering context.
component.ConfigFileListEntry: ConfigFileListEntry represents an element of derived.configFileList.
component.ConfigMapVolume: ConfigMapVolume represents a configMap volume source.
component.ConfigurationItems: ConfigurationItems contains environment and file configurations.
component.ConnectionItem: ConnectionItem represents a single connection with its target metadata and resolved env vars.
component.ConnectionsContextData:
ConnectionsContextData is the template context representation of dependencies. It exposes
per-item views (Items, Resources) plus merged flat lists (EnvVars, VolumeMounts, Volumes)
for templates that want a single combined surface.

	${dependencies.items}        — endpoint per-item view
	${dependencies.resources}    — resource per-item view
	${dependencies.envVars}      — merged across endpoints + resources
	${dependencies.volumeMounts} — merged across resources
	${dependencies.volumes}      — merged across resources
component.ConnectionsData:
ConnectionsData contains the per-item dependency views (endpoint connections and resource
dependencies) that the controller resolves before invoking the pipeline. This is the input
type used in RenderInput and context inputs.
component.ContainerConfigurations: ContainerConfigurations contains configs and secrets for a container.
component.DataPlaneData: DataPlaneData provides data plane configuration in templates.
component.DataPlaneData.annotations:
Annotations are the DataPlane's metadata.annotations, surfaced verbatim so templates
can read platform-set hints from the data plane. Read defensively, e.g.
has(dataplane.annotations) && "key" in dataplane.annotations, since the map is absent
when the DataPlane has no annotations.
component.DerivedContext:
DerivedContext holds precomputed derived views of configurations, workload,
and dependency data. CEL macros rewrite helper method calls (e.g.
configurations.toConfigFileList()) to field selects on this struct
(e.g. derived.configFileList), eliminating runtime map[string]any traversal.
component.DerivedContext.endpointResources:
EndpointResources backs the workload.toEndpointResources() macro. Always a
non-nil map (possibly empty) so the macro's optional index evaluates even when
no endpoint produced resources; omitting the key would fail the field select
with "no such key" instead of yielding optional.none.
component.EnvConfiguration:
EnvConfiguration represents an environment variable configuration.
Value is always emitted (no omitempty) so that empty-string literals survive
the JSON round-trip into the CEL evaluation context.
component.EnvFromEntry: EnvFromEntry represents an element of derived.containerEnvFrom.
component.EnvVarEntry:
EnvVarEntry mirrors corev1.EnvVar for the subset of shapes the platform emits when
merging endpoint connection env vars and resource dependency env vars into
${dependencies.envVars}. JSON-compatible with corev1.EnvVar so the rendered Pod spec is
unchanged.
component.EnvVarSourceEntry: EnvVarSourceEntry mirrors corev1.EnvVarSource for the two ref kinds the platform emits.
component.EnvironmentData:
EnvironmentData provides environment-specific gateway configuration in templates.
If the environment does not have gateway configuration, values fallback to DataPlane gateway.
component.EnvsByContainerEntry: EnvsByContainerEntry represents an element of derived.configEnvs or derived.secretEnvs.
component.GatewayData: GatewayData provides gateway configuration in templates.
component.GatewayEndpointData: GatewayEndpointData provides endpoint data for a gateway in templates.
component.GatewayListenerData: GatewayListenerData provides listener data for a gateway in templates.
component.GatewayNetworkData: GatewayNetworkData provides traffic gateway data for ingress/egress in templates.
component.KeyRef: KeyRef references a single key within a Secret or ConfigMap.
component.MetadataContext:
MetadataContext provides structured metadata for resource generation.
This is computed by the controller and passed to the renderer.
component.MetadataContext.annotations: Annotations are common annotations to add to all resources.
component.MetadataContext.componentName:
ComponentName is the name of the component.
Example: "my-service"
component.MetadataContext.componentNamespace:
ComponentNamespace is the namespace on which the component is created.
Example: "cp-acme-corp"
component.MetadataContext.componentUID:
ComponentUID is the unique identifier of the component.
Example: "a1b2c3d4-5678-90ab-cdef-1234567890ab"
component.MetadataContext.dataPlaneName:
DataPlaneName is the name of the data plane.
Example: "my-dataplane"
component.MetadataContext.dataPlaneUID:
DataPlaneUID is the unique identifier of the data plane.
Example: "c3d4e5f6-7890-12cd-ef01-34567890abcd"
component.MetadataContext.environmentName:
EnvironmentName is the name of the environment.
Example: "production"
component.MetadataContext.environmentUID:
EnvironmentUID is the unique identifier of the environment.
Example: "d4e5f6g7-8901-23de-f012-4567890abcde"
component.MetadataContext.labels:
Labels are common labels to add to all resources.
Example: {"openchoreo.dev/component": "my-service", ...}
component.MetadataContext.name:
Name is the base name to use for generated resources.
Example: "my-service-dev-a1b2c3d4"
component.MetadataContext.namespace:
Namespace is the target namespace for the resources.
Example: "dp-acme-corp-payment-dev-x1y2z3w4"
component.MetadataContext.podSelectors:
PodSelectors are platform-injected selectors for pod identity.
Used in Deployment selectors, Service selectors, etc.
Example: {
  "openchoreo.dev/namespace": "dp-acme-corp-payment-dev-x1y2z3w4",
  "openchoreo.dev/project": "acme-corp",
  "openchoreo.dev/component": "payment",
  "openchoreo.dev/environment": "dev",
  "openchoreo.dev/component-uid": "abc123",
  "openchoreo.dev/environment-uid": "dev",
  "openchoreo.dev/project-uid": "xyz789",
}
component.MetadataContext.projectName:
ProjectName is the name of the project.
Example: "my-project"
component.MetadataContext.projectUID:
ProjectUID is the unique identifier of the project.
Example: "b2c3d4e5-6789-01bc-def0-234567890abc"
component.NameRef: NameRef is a reference containing a name field.
component.ObservabilityPlaneRefData: ObservabilityPlaneRefData provides observability plane reference in templates.
component.RemoteRefData: RemoteRefData contains remote reference data for secrets.
component.ResourceDependencyItem:
ResourceDependencyItem represents a single resource dependency with its target metadata
and pre-computed env vars, volume mounts, and volumes for the consuming container.
Mirrors ConnectionItem's role on the endpoint side.
component.SchemaBundle:
SchemaBundle holds both structural and JSON schemas for validation workflows.
The structural schema is used for defaulting, while the JSON schema
is used for validation.
component.SchemaInput: SchemaInput contains schema information for building structural and JSON schemas.
component.SecretFileListEntry: SecretFileListEntry represents an element of derived.secretFileList.
component.SecretVolume: SecretVolume represents a secret volume source.
component.ServicePortEntry: ServicePortEntry represents an element of derived.servicePorts.
component.TraitContext:
TraitContext represents the evaluated context for rendering trait resources.
This is the output of BuildTraitContext and is used by the template engine.
component.TraitContext.configurations:
Configurations are extracted configuration items from workload.
Contains configs and secrets for the single container.
Accessed via ${configurations.configs.envs}, ${configurations.secrets.files}, etc.
component.TraitContext.dataplane:
DataPlane provides data plane configuration.
Accessed via ${dataplane.secretStore}, ${dataplane.gateway.ingress.external.https.host}, etc.
component.TraitContext.dependencies:
Dependencies contains dependency metadata and merged env vars for templates.
Accessed via ${dependencies.items} and ${dependencies.envVars}.
component.TraitContext.derived: Derived holds precomputed views that CEL macros resolve to via field selects.
component.TraitContext.environment:
Environment provides environment-specific gateway configuration.
Accessed via ${environment.gateway.ingress.external.https.host}, etc.
Falls back to DataPlane gateway values if Environment.Gateway is not configured.
component.TraitContext.environmentConfigs:
EnvironmentConfigs from ReleaseBinding.Spec.TraitEnvironmentConfigs[instanceName], pruned to Trait.Spec.EnvironmentConfigs schema.
Accessed via ${environmentConfigs.*}
component.TraitContext.gateway:
Gateway provides the effective gateway configuration for this deployment.
Uses environment gateway if configured, falls back to DataPlane gateway.
Accessed via ${gateway.ingress.external.https.host}, etc.
component.TraitContext.metadata:
Metadata provides structured naming and labeling information.
Accessed via ${metadata.name}, ${metadata.namespace}, ${metadata.componentName}, etc.
component.TraitContext.parameters:
Parameters from TraitInstance.Parameters, pruned to Trait.Spec.Parameters schema.
Accessed via ${parameters.*}
component.TraitContext.trait:
Trait contains trait-specific metadata.
Accessed via ${trait.name}, ${trait.instanceName}
component.TraitContext.workload:
Workload contains workload specification (container, endpoints).
Accessed via ${workload.container}, ${workload.endpoints}
component.TraitContextBase:
TraitContextBase contains the inputs common to building both regular and embedded trait
contexts (metadata, dataplane, environment, workload data, configurations, dependencies,
notification channel). Pipeline callers typically build this once at the start of a render
and embed it in each TraitContextInput / EmbeddedTraitContextInput inside the trait loops.
component.TraitContextInput:
TraitContextInput contains all inputs needed to build a trait rendering context.

Both component-level and embedded traits use this input. The only difference is how
callers obtain the resolved parameter and environmentConfigs maps:
  - Component-level traits: use ExtractTraitInstanceBindings to deserialize the
    ComponentTrait instance and ReleaseBinding override.
  - Embedded traits: use ResolveEmbeddedTraitBindings to evaluate CEL expressions
    against the component context.

By the time the input reaches BuildTraitContext both flows look identical.
component.TraitMetadata.instanceName:
InstanceName is the unique instance name within the component.
Example: "my-storage"
component.TraitMetadata.name:
Name is the name of the trait.
Example: "storage"
component.VolumeEntry: VolumeEntry represents an element of derived.volumes.
component.VolumeMountEntry: VolumeMountEntry represents an element of derived.containerVolumeMounts.
component.WorkloadData: WorkloadData contains workload information for templates.

project.BaseContext:
BaseContext is the top-level CEL surface produced by buildBaseContext and
fed into the template engine.
project.BaseContext.gateway:
Gateway is the effective gateway (Environment.Gateway, which itself is
env-or-dp merged) exposed at the top level for terseness:
${gateway.egress.external.https.host} is identical to
${environment.gateway.egress.external.https.host}.

Templates that may evaluate against a missing gateway must guard via
has(environment.gateway) — has(gateway) is invalid CEL because the
top-level alias is omitted from the marshaled map when nil.
project.DataPlaneContext:
DataPlaneContext is the dataplane surface exposed to CEL templates as
${dataplane.*}. Optional fields use omitempty so templates can guard with
has(...) — mirrors the resource pipeline's contract.
project.DataPlaneContext.gateway:
Gateway is the raw DataPlane-level gateway configuration. Nil when the
DataPlane has no gateway configured. The effective gateway used by most
templates is the merged Environment-or-DataPlane value exposed at the
top-level ${gateway.*} and on ${environment.gateway.*}.
project.DataPlaneContext.observabilityPlaneRef:
ObservabilityPlaneRef is the observability plane reference for
ProjectTypes that emit observability-plane-side resources. Optional; nil
when the DataPlane has no observability plane configured. Templates that
reference ${dataplane.observabilityPlaneRef.*} must guard with
has(dataplane.observabilityPlaneRef).
project.DataPlaneContext.secretStore:
SecretStore is the name of the ESO ClusterSecretStore configured on the
DataPlane. ProjectTypes emitting a shared-cell ExternalSecret reference
this.
project.EnvironmentContext:
EnvironmentContext is the per-environment surface exposed to CEL templates
as ${environment.*}. Gateway carries the merged effective gateway:
environment-level overrides take precedence, falling back to dataplane-level
values at each leaf. Mirrors the resource pipeline's EnvironmentContext.
project.GatewayData: GatewayData provides gateway configuration in templates.
project.GatewayEndpointData: GatewayEndpointData provides endpoint data for a gateway in templates.
project.GatewayListenerData: GatewayListenerData provides listener data for a gateway in templates.
project.GatewayNetworkData:
GatewayNetworkData provides traffic gateway data for ingress/egress in
templates.
project.MetadataContext:
MetadataContext is the platform-injected metadata surface exposed to CEL
templates as ${metadata.*}. The controller computes every field before
calling the pipeline. JSON tags determine the CEL-facing field names when
the context is marshaled via structToMap.
project.MetadataContext.annotations: Annotations are propagated from the ProjectReleaseBinding CR.
project.MetadataContext.labels:
Labels are platform-injected standard labels. PE templates that
propagate ${metadata.labels} get consistent labeling across every
rendered DP-side object.
project.MetadataContext.projectNamespace:
ProjectNamespace is the control-plane namespace where the
ProjectReleaseBinding lives.
project.ObservabilityPlaneRefContext:
ObservabilityPlaneRefContext is the {kind, name} reference exposed under
${dataplane.observabilityPlaneRef.*}.
project.Pipeline:
Pipeline renders the inlined (Cluster)ProjectType.spec.resources templates
for a single ProjectReleaseBinding. The instance holds a template.Engine
whose CEL environment and program caches are reused across calls; consumers
(binding controller, future CLI) instantiate one Pipeline and reuse it.
project.RenderInput:
RenderInput carries everything Render needs. The binding controller
rehydrates ProjectTypeSpec and ProjectParameters from the immutable
ProjectRelease snapshot and supplies EnvironmentConfigs from the binding.
project.RenderOutput:
RenderOutput carries the rendered manifests in spec order. ForEach
templates contribute one entry per iteration, with ID suffixed by the
iteration index.
project.RenderedEntry:
RenderedEntry is one rendered manifest. The controller marshals Object
into runtime.RawExtension at its own boundary so the pipeline stays free
of K8s runtime types in its public surface.

resource.BaseContext:
BaseContext is the top-level CEL surface produced by buildBaseContext and
fed into the template engine. withApplied layers applied.<id>.status.* on
top of it for output and readyWhen evaluation. The struct exists so the
pipeline and the validation package share a single source of truth for the
CEL surface — validation reflects on BaseContext to declare CEL variables;
the pipeline JSON-marshals it via structToMap for runtime evaluation.
resource.BaseContext.gateway:
Gateway is the effective gateway (Environment.Gateway, which itself
is env-or-dp merged) exposed at the top level for terseness:
${gateway.ingress.external.https.host} is identical to
${environment.gateway.ingress.external.https.host}.

Unlike Environment.Gateway/DataPlane.Gateway, this field is always
non-nil (buildBaseContext substitutes an empty &GatewayData{} when
Environment.Gateway is nil) so the "gateway" CEL variable is always
declared and has(gateway.ingress...) can be used directly without
first guarding has(gateway) — a bare, undeclared "gateway" identifier
would otherwise fail to *compile*, not just evaluate false.
resource.DataPlaneContext:
DataPlaneContext is the dataplane surface exposed to CEL templates as
${dataplane.*}. Optional fields use omitempty so templates can guard with
has(...) — mirrors the component pipeline's contract.
resource.DataPlaneContext.gateway:
Gateway is the raw DataPlane-level gateway configuration. Templates
emitting HTTPRoute / Ingress against the DP gateway reference it via
${dataplane.gateway.ingress.external.https.host} etc. Nil when the
DataPlane has no gateway configured. The effective gateway used by
most templates is the merged Environment-or-DataPlane value exposed
at the top-level ${gateway.*} and on ${environment.gateway.*}.
resource.DataPlaneContext.observabilityPlaneRef:
ObservabilityPlaneRef is the observability plane reference for
ResourceTypes that emit observability-plane-side resources (alert
rules, dashboards). Optional; nil when the DataPlane has no
observability plane configured. PE templates that reference
${dataplane.observabilityPlaneRef.*} must guard with
has(dataplane.observabilityPlaneRef).
resource.DataPlaneContext.secretStore:
SecretStore is the name of the ESO ClusterSecretStore configured on
the DataPlane. ResourceTypes emitting ExternalSecret reference this.
resource.EnvironmentContext:
EnvironmentContext is the per-environment surface exposed to CEL templates
as ${environment.*}. Gateway carries the merged effective gateway:
environment-level overrides take precedence, falling back to dataplane-level
values at each leaf. Mirrors the component pipeline's EnvironmentData
(the resource side omits DefaultNotificationChannel — that field is
alert-routing-specific and not relevant to the managed-infra surface).
resource.GatewayData: GatewayData provides gateway configuration in templates.
resource.GatewayEndpointData: GatewayEndpointData provides endpoint data for a gateway in templates.
resource.GatewayListenerData: GatewayListenerData provides listener data for a gateway in templates.
resource.GatewayNetworkData:
GatewayNetworkData provides traffic gateway data for ingress/egress in
templates.
resource.MetadataContext:
MetadataContext is the platform-injected metadata surface exposed to CEL
templates as ${metadata.*}. The controller computes every field before
calling the pipeline. JSON tags determine the CEL-facing field names when
the context is marshaled via structToMap, and are also reflected on by the
validation package to declare the CEL env surface.
resource.MetadataContext.annotations: Annotations are propagated from the Resource CR.
resource.MetadataContext.labels:
Labels are platform-injected standard labels (openchoreo.dev/resource,
openchoreo.dev/project, openchoreo.dev/environment, plus matching
*-uid keys). PE templates that propagate ${metadata.labels} get
consistent labeling across every rendered DP-side object.
resource.MetadataContext.name:
Name is the platform-computed base name for rendered resources,
shaped {resource}-{env}-{hash} (mirrors component pipeline's
{component}-{env}-{hash} convention).
resource.MetadataContext.namespace:
Namespace is the DP-side project-env mapped namespace. Exposed via
CEL only; the pipeline does NOT force-set metadata.namespace on
rendered manifests.
resource.MetadataContext.resourceNamespace: ResourceNamespace is the CP namespace where the Resource CR lives.
resource.ObservabilityPlaneRefContext:
ObservabilityPlaneRefContext is the {kind, name} reference exposed under
${dataplane.observabilityPlaneRef.*}.
resource.Pipeline:
Pipeline orchestrates ResourceType template rendering and output resolution
for a single ResourceReleaseBinding. The instance holds a template.Engine
whose CEL environment and program caches are reused across calls; consumers
(controller, webhook, future CLI) instantiate one Pipeline and reuse it.
resource.RenderInput:
RenderInput carries everything RenderManifests, ResolveOutputs, and
EvaluateReadyWhen need. Inputs are typed CRDs (mirrors the component
pipeline at internal/pipeline/component/types.go:21-65). The binding
controller rehydrates ResourceType and Resource from the immutable
ResourceRelease snapshot before calling; webhooks pass live CRDs
directly.
resource.RenderOutput: RenderOutput carries the rendered manifests in spec order.
resource.RenderedEntry:
RenderedEntry is one rendered manifest. The controller marshals Object
into runtime.RawExtension at its own boundary so the pipeline stays free
of K8s runtime types in its public surface.
resource.ResolvedOutput:
ResolvedOutput is one entry resolved from ResourceTypeSpec.Outputs. Exactly
one of Value, SecretKeyRef, or ConfigMapKeyRef is populated, matching the
source kind declared on the ResourceType output.

workflow.Pipeline:
Pipeline orchestrates workflow rendering by combining WorkflowRun,
Workflow to generate fully resolved resources (e.g., Argo Workflow).
workflow.RenderInput: RenderInput contains all required inputs for workflow rendering.
workflow.RenderMetadata: RenderMetadata contains non-fatal information about the rendering process.
workflow.RenderOutput: RenderOutput contains the rendered workflow resource and associated metadata.
workflow.RenderedResource: RenderedResource represents a rendered Kubernetes resource with its identifier.
workflow.WorkflowContext:
WorkflowContext provides contextual metadata for workflow rendering.
These values are injected into CEL expressions as ${metadata.*} variables.
workflow.WorkflowPlaneData: WorkflowPlaneData contains workflow plane configuration exposed to CEL templates.
